content.user_title: Build GPU Sliders and Galleries with gpuslider
content.value_statement: GPU sliders require coordinated rendering, layouts, and framework integration. This skill guides gpuslider setup with visual plugins, CSS sizing, and browser fallbacks.
actual_capabilities: Guide package installation and plain JavaScript slider initialization with controls and keyboard plugins.
Provide React and Next.js integration examples using Slider and Slide components.
Select single-slide transitions, carousel layouts, and effects that respond to movement or pointer position.
Explain responsive slide spacing and sizing through CSS variables or layout options.
Identify the lightbox plugin and its import path.
Explain cross-origin image requirements, stable slide dimensions, and plugin recreation in React.
limitations: This skill provides integration instructions, not the gpuslider runtime or a bundled application.
Advanced options require reading the documentation shipped with the installed package.
Cross-origin images require appropriate CORS headers for canvas rendering.
GPU rendering depends on browser support; the documented fallbacks do not guarantee identical visual effects.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Slider
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gpuslider to add a two-image JavaScript slider with controls and keyboard navigation. Set stable slide dimensions and include the required stylesheet.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Responsive Carousel
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a responsive gpuslider carousel without stack mode. Configure slides per view and gaps through CSS, and add the documented stretch effect.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate React Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate gpuslider into my Next.js gallery using Slider and Slide. Read the installed documentation before choosing advanced props, and explain plugin recreation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Effects and Browser Fallbacks
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a gpuslider gallery with liquid transitions and a lightbox. Check the installed documentation, CORS requirements, stable sizing, and WebGPU, WebGL, and script-free fallbacks.

output_examples.input: Recommend a single-image slider with a liquid transition.
output: Use stack mode with the liquid effect in the canvas plugin.
Set slide height or aspect ratio through CSS.

output_examples.input: My cross-origin gallery images do not work in the canvas.
output: Use anonymous cross-origin loading and verify that the image server sends compatible CORS headers.
Serve images from the same origin if the remote server cannot provide those headers.

output_examples.input: How should I update plugins in a React gallery?
output: The plugins prop is read when the slider is created.
Use the remake dependency list to recreate the slider when relevant dependencies change.
Confirm advanced lifecycle options in the installed package documentation.

best_practices: Read the installed package documentation before using options or effect names beyond the examples.
Keep slide dimensions stable through CSS height or aspect ratio, with responsive spacing.
Verify image CORS configuration and test rendering fallbacks in target browsers.
anti_patterns: Guessing undocumented option names or effects.
Sizing or moving slide elements through scripts instead of the supported layout configuration.
Assuming React plugin changes apply automatically without recreating the slider.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers plain JavaScript, React, and Next.js integration with gpuslider.

faq.question: Does this skill include the slider library?
faq.answer: No. The instructions require installing the gpuslider npm package separately.

faq.question: What happens when WebGPU is unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill describes WebGL 2 and page-based fallbacks. Without scripts, slides scroll and snap.

faq.question: Can I use images from another domain?
faq.answer: Yes, but canvas rendering requires anonymous cross-origin loading and compatible server headers. Same-origin images avoid this requirement.

faq.question: Where can I find the complete API?
faq.answer: Read DOCS.md inside the installed gpuslider package. The skill also links to the project documentation website.

faq.question: Can React plugins change after initialization?
faq.answer: Plugins are read during creation. Use the remake prop with relevant dependencies to recreate the slider when needed.
